findings.title: Segment-aware address discovery requirement has no mechanism, owner, or meaningful test coverage
findings.evidence: KEP README.md lines 156, 381, 505 impose 'discovery must publish only the aligned base-group target; no residual or surge identities', but no section assigns an owner or mechanism (every other integration names exact entry points, e.g. line 665 for the Adapter). Today discovery is built by the RBG controller via discovery.NewConfigBuilder (rolebasedgroup_controller.go:492) and enumerates dense ordinals [0, spec.roles[].replicas) (pkg/discovery/config_builder.go buildInstances/memberOrdinals) — an unaligned desired state (2P:1D with P=5,D=2) would publish the residual prefill-4 address that will never be created, reintroducing issue #543's 'partial deployment / occupied resources / unusable service' failure mode. Test plan: exactly one unit bullet (line 1116), zero integration/e2e bullets.
findings.proposedFix: Add a design subsection naming the discovery entry point (RBG controller discovery step / pkg/discovery/config_builder.go), specify the source of truth (last valid applied base-group target vs current RBG spec) for the misaligned case, and add integration + e2e test-plan bullets for Segment-aware discovery.

findings.title: Static webhook rule segBatchSize >= minSegments over-rejects valid steady-state configurations
findings.evidence: README.md 'Configuration Validation with Scaling': a rule with scaling+Gang must satisfy B >= G unconditionally at admission, justified only by the from-zero / below-threshold first batch. For an RBG already running C >= G groups, B < G is safe, but the webhook still rejects it — permanently coupling scale-out batch granularity to the gang threshold (users wanting one-group-at-a-time additions on a mature gang-protected workload must add >= G groups per batch). Design decision is documented as stateless-by-choice; raised as a question, not a defect.
findings.proposedFix: Either accept and document the steady-state over-rejection explicitly, or move the check to reconciliation where the current applied group count C is known (reject only when C < G and B < G).

findings.title: Scale-in below minSegments: user-visible outcome not stated
findings.evidence: README.md says an Adapter 'reducing desired groups below minSegments' is reported 'through the existing incompatible-Gang path' — but the existing path (rolebasedgroup_controller.go:253-276) does more than report: it returns early and leaves roles untouched, halting role reconciliation entirely. So the scale-in is blocked (RIS stays at the old target) until the user fixes the config. The doc never states this user-visible outcome; a reader could equally conclude the scale-in proceeds with a warning. The integration-test bullet 'reports the configuration error without adjusting replicas' is ambiguous between 'no auto-raise' and 'blocks the scale-in'.
findings.proposedFix: State explicitly: scale-in below minSegments blocks member reconciliation (roles left untouched) until configuration is corrected, mirroring the existing incompatible-Gang semantics.

findings.title: Rule rename rewrites fleet-wide segment labels; gang subGroup partition transiently splits
findings.evidence: ruleID = SHA-256(ruleName)[:12], so renaming a rule (allowed when the ratio is unchanged) changes every RI/Pod segment + segment-rule label value and re-keys the Volcano matchLabelKeys=[segment] subGroup partition. Until synchronization converges, pods of the same logical group carry different segment values, splitting subGroups; the PodGroup threshold (minSubGroups x subGroupSize) may be unsatisfiable in that window, stalling gang dispatch. The doc allows 'temporary cross-layer inconsistency' generically but never calls out the gang-threshold interaction during rename, and no test bullet covers rename under an active gang.
findings.proposedFix: Add a boundary note (rename converges asynchronously and gang dispatch may stall during the window) plus a test-plan bullet for rename with an active gang PodGroup.
